reviews.body:
Approving. This is a real break, not a hypothetical one.

`response.content[0].text` holds only while the first block is a text block. With thinking enabled the response leads with a `thinking` block, so `content[0]` has no `.text` and the call raises — or, worse on models that return a summarized thinking block, silently returns reasoning text as if it were the answer. Joining only blocks whose `type == "text"` is the documented way to read these responses.

`getattr(block, "type", None)` rather than `block.type` is the right call too: it degrades to skipping an unexpected block instead of raising on one that lacks the attribute.

The test constructs the response with `SimpleNamespace` and puts a `thinking` block ahead of the text, which reproduces the actual shape rather than mocking the method under test. It fails against the old `content[0].text`.

Worth noting for whoever picks up the related work: the same `content[0]` assumption may exist on other Anthropic call sites in this file (streaming, or any tool-use path). Not this PR's job, but a grep for `content[0]` would be worth a follow-up.
